searches_run: Schiebinger 2019 optimal transport analysis single cell gene expression identifies developmental trajectories Cell
Weinreb 2020 lineage tracing on transcriptional landscapes links state to fate Science

proposals.title: Test temporal population reweighting before expression dynamics
proposals.claim: Training-only temporal reweighting of shared broad cell states, with frozen within-state expression, reduces held-out-stage mmd_u versus nearest-stage resampling.
proposals.mechanism: Changing population weights changes the aggregate expression distribution and may lower mmd_u. Compare de_direction under frozen and evolving conditional expression to diagnose whether aggregate shifts require within-state changes; neither establishes lineage.
proposals.falsifier: On the first eligible held-out-stage embryo split, reject if the paired mean mmd_u improvement is nonpositive under matched cell counts and repeated random sampling; no target labels enter fitting.

evidence.says: Separately names abundance and conditioned expression as prediction targets; lineage is also listed but lacks tracing evidence.
The diagnostic proxy takes at most 150 leading cells; no randomized or embryo-aware sampling appears here.
Temporal coupling needs assumptions; growth and death change mass, and expression snapshots do not directly observe joint ancestry.

peer_responses.on: neuralode-r1-2: distinguish solver convergence and temporal predictive validity
peer_responses.because: Endorse the distinction; mmd_u/de_direction validate marginals, not ancestry. Schiebinger 2019 requires coupling assumptions; Weinreb 2020 finds fate biases hidden from expression. Add independent clonal fate and growth/death tests before lineage claims.

declined: Hard lineage-tree constraints: unpaired expression snapshots do not identify ancestry; a plausible movie or improved marginal score cannot validate a developmental mechanism.
